title: Support Examples Index

handoffCard.label: Support Examples Quickstart
handoffCard.useWhen: Use during a live maintainer handoff when an incoming report needs a 60-second route to the right support artifacts.

installedPackageProvenance.label: Installed Package Support Examples
installedPackageProvenance.useWhen: Use when a maintainer needs to verify or open the support examples from an installed npm package instead of a repository checkout.
installedPackageProvenance.verifyCommand: npm explore memento-mori-jester -- npm run pack:contents:check

releaseProvenanceGate.label: Release Support Provenance Gate
releaseProvenanceGate.useWhen: Use after npm publish succeeds so the release closeout records installed-package support verification from package-relative artifacts.
releaseProvenanceGate.verifyCommand: npm explore memento-mori-jester -- npm run pack:contents:check
recordFields: repo-only paths confirmed absent or not required

artifacts.label: Support Lifecycle Map
artifacts.useWhen: Use when you need the shortest scan of the support path before reading detailed checklists.
requiredMarkers: report -> triage -> response -> closeout -> prioritization -> backlog-record -> backlog-review

artifacts.label: Support Lifecycle Worksheet
artifacts.useWhen: Use during an active review of one public support report when each stage needs concrete fields to record.

artifacts.label: Filled Support Lifecycle Worksheet Example
artifacts.useWhen: Use when comparing an active report with one completed synthetic docs-example path from report through backlog review.

quickPath.maintainerQuestion: Is the report redacted, minimal, and safe to discuss publicly?
Is this expected docs behavior, fixture backlog, or rule-review work?
Which checked public-safe reply should go back to the reporter?
Did the immediate support decision ship, queue, or open follow-up?
Is the follow-up low-priority docs, medium fixture work, or high rule review?
Is there a public-safe backlog artifact with evidence and checks?
Does the item remain active, or should it close with no action?

requiredPublicSafeMarkers: placeholder links are used for public issue and follow-up links
SECURITY.md redirects sensitive reports away from public issues
no secrets, private code, private paths, customer data, full logs, unredacted SARIF, package publishing credentials, MCP data exposure, or exploitable security details
privacyGuardrail: Keep support examples public-safe: label synthetic material, use placeholders, avoid secrets and private details, and route credential exposure, package publishing compromise, MCP data exposure, command execution risk, or exploitable security details through SECURITY.md.
